sentences.text: 1. Accused no.2 in Crime No.322/2023 registered by Sarjapura Police Station, Bengaluru District,
for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 302, 304B, 34 IPC,
is before this Court under Section 438 Cr.PC.

2. Heard the learned Counsel for the parties.
3. Based on the complaint of Ajay Gosh who is the father of deceased Bhanupriya, Sarjapura police station, Bengaluru District had registered FIR in Crime No.322/2023 against Keshava and the petitioner herein for the aforesaid offences.
Accused no.1 - Keshava is the son of the petitioner and deceased Bhanupriya was the wife of accused no.1 and their marriage was performed in the month of June 2020.
Apprehending arrest in the said case, petitioner had filed Crl. Misc. No.5461/2023 before the Court of III Addl. District & Sessions Judge, Anekal, which was rejected on 21.10.2023.

entities.text: III Addl. District & Sessions Judge, Anekal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Therefore, she is before this Court.
4. Learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is a aged lady and she is residing separately.
There is no serious allegation against the petitioner in the complaint.
NC: 2023:KHC:46174 Accused no.1 is arrested and is in custody from 23.09.2023.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.
5. Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the petition.
6. From a reading of the complaint averments, it is seen that no such serious allegations are made against the petitioner herein who is the mother of accused no.1 - Keshava.
The marriage of Keshava with deceased Bhanupriya was performed in the month of June 2020.

There is no such material in the complaint which would go to show that the petitioner herein had demanded dowry and had ill-treated the deceased in furtherance of such demand and as a result, the deceased had committed suicide.
Petitioner is aged about 55 years and it is submitted by the learned Counsel for the petitioner that she is residing separately.
Accused no.1 who is the husband of deceased is in custody.
Under the circumstances, I am of the opinion that the prayer made by the petitioner for grant of anticipatory bail is required to be answered affirmatively.

Accordingly, the following order:
Papathi vs State Of Karnataka on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172432254/
2 7.
The petition is allowed.

The respondent - Police or any other police in the State of Karnataka are directed to release NC: 2023:KHC:46174 the petitioner in the event of her arrest in Crime No.322/2023 registered by Sarjapura Police Station, Bengaluru District, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 302, 304B, 34 IPC, subject to the following conditions:
1. The Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of the copy of this order and shall execute a personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the investigating officer.
2. Petitioner shall regularly appear before the Trial Court without fail unless exempted by the Trial Court for valid reasons.
3. Petitioner shall not tamper with the prosecution witness and she shall co-operate with the police for investigation and appear before them whenever called upon.

SD/-
